Q: With vb.net, how can I split this filename/string? A:

A solution with Regex

Imports System.Text.RegularExpressions
Module Module1
    Sub Main()
        Dim suffix As String = "_version"
        Dim filename As String = "Something_version1.jpg"
        Dim regex As Regex = New Regex(".*" & suffix, RegexOptions.IgnoreCase)
        Dim result As Match = regex.Match(filename)
        Debug.Print(result.Value)
    End Sub

End Module

The regular expression

*. matches any character zero or more times, as many times as possible, giving characters back as needed (greedy)
suffix variable contains a string to match literally and make the search dynamic.
RegexOptions.IgnoreCase set the option flag to case insensitive (if you need it).

Q: java.lang.NoClassDefFoundError:failed resolution of :Lorg/apache/http/ProtocolVersion A:

I have faced this issue since I updated AGP - 8.5.1. In my case, the debug app was working fine. But the signed app was not working.

I have set the below value appropriately.

Only at app level build.gradle/build.gradle.kts file parameter should be - minifyEnabled true / isMinifyEnabled = true.

Sub-modules - build.gradle/build.gradle.kts file parameter should be - minifyEnabled false / isMinifyEnabled = false.

Q: MySQL DISTINCT on a GROUP_CONCAT() A:

If you DBMS doesn't support SEPARATOR, you can write:

SELECT GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT(categories) || '\n') FROM table

Q: How does a blank __init__.py change the behavior of import in python? A:

As described in this article https://realpython.com/python-init-py/ :
The difference between using and not using an __init__.py is that the module gets treated as a namespace package vs a regular packages and
"it’s the namespace prefix, not the physical directory, that identifies the package contents"

if in your __init__.py you include a from .b import something
You should be able to go a.something in your code.

Q: Database partitioning - Horizontal vs Vertical - Difference between Normalization and Row Splitting? A:

Horizontal Partitioning in a database

Keeping all the fields.

E.G.: Table Employees has fields id, name, email, designation and phone.

E.G. 1: Keeping all the fields and distributing records over multiple machines. E.G. id range 1-100000 or 100000-200000 records in each machine and distributing over multiple machines.

E.G. 2: Keeping separate databases for regions. E.G.: Asia Pacific, North America.

Key: Picking the set of rows based on a criteria.

Vertical Partitioning in a database

It is similar to Normalization where the same table is divided in to multiple tables and used with joins if required.

E.G.: id, name, and designation are put in one table while phone and email, which may not be frequently accessed, are put in another.

Key: Picking set of columns based on a criteria.

Horizontal/Vertical Scaling is different from partitioning

Horizontal Scaling is about adding more machines to enable improved responsiveness and availability of any system including database.The idea is to distribute the work load to multiple machines.

Vertical Scaling is about adding more capability in the form of CPU or Memory to an existing machine or machines to enable improved responsiveness and availability of any system, including database. In a virtual machine setup it can be configured virtually instead of adding real physical machines/memory.

Q: View query results from a PL/SQL block without PUT_LINE, RETURN_RESULTS, or CREATE? A:

The issue is that SELECT QTest(v_ID) FROM DUAL returns the ref cursor as one opaque column, not an expanded rowset which only works when a client explicitly binds a REF CURSOR OUT param, not from a plain SELECT.

Since you can't create objects, skip ref cursors entirely and use dbms_xmlgen + XMLTABLE to turn your dynamic SQL into XML, then shred it back into a normal rowset in the same statement. If you are using oracle-12.1, just build the SQL string directly inside getxmltype() instead

Q: VB.NET and catia A:

I think the problem is AddFromSel(). This does not really measure the 2 selected faces, it creates a distance using the selected products. So if the two parts touch anywhere, the minimum distance is correctly 0 mm.

Also GetMinimumDistance() without context is not good for faces from different CATProduct instances, because their local coordinates/transformation can be different.

I would remove method 1 and 2 and only use the in-context version:

Dim spa As Object = GetSPAWorkbench()

Dim measurable As Object =
    spa.GetMeasurableInContext(ref1, item1.LeafProduct)

Dim distance As Double =
    CDbl(measurable.GetMinimumDistanceInContext(
        ref2,
        item2.LeafProduct
    ))

Return distance

GetMeasurableInContext and GetMinimumDistanceInContext are specifically meant to measure geometry inside a Product with the instance transformations applied.

Also don't leave the Catch blocks empty while debugging. You may currently have an exception in method 3 and never see it:

Catch ex As Exception
    MessageBox.Show(ex.ToString())
End Try

You can also call GetMinimumDistancePointsInContext to see which actual points CATIA is using. That will quickly show if CATIA is still measuring the complete parts instead of the faces.
